identity.name: Sodium phosphates
identity.chemical_class: Inorganic sodium salts of phosphoric acid (orthophosphates)

function.mechanism: Controls pH through phosphate buffering and supports formulation stability via ion sequestration and emulsification functions.

adi.basis: Group ADI for phosphates expressed as phosphorus (E338-341, E343, E450-452).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation set a group ADI of 40 mg/kg bw/day (as phosphorus) and reported ADI exceedance in infants/toddlers/children at mean exposure and in adolescents at high exposure.

adi.basis: Group MTDI for phosphorus from all sources, expressed as P.

concerns.summary: EFSA reported ADI exceedance in several younger population groups and noted that the ADI does not apply to individuals with moderate-to-severe renal impairment.
Prospective cohort evidence linked higher urinary phosphate (a potential marker of high processed-food phosphate intake) with higher cardiovascular disease incidence.
A mouse study reported anxiety-like behavior and neuroimmune changes after chronic high-phosphate diet exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA reported no concern for genotoxicity and carcinogenicity for the phosphate additive group.
EFSA reported no developmental toxicity concern in reviewed studies.
FDA lists sodium phosphate as GRAS under GMP conditions in 21 CFR 182.1778.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported exceedance against its 40 mg/kg bw/day group ADI in multiple population groups in analytical-data scenarios and noted supplement-related exceedance.

risk_assessment.rationale: E339 remains approved in major jurisdictions, but EFSA's current health-based guidance value is exceeded in several younger populations and high consumers, and additional human/epidemiologic literature supports concern at higher inorganic phosphate exposure patterns.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI of 40 mg/kg bw/day (as phosphorus)
EFSA-reported ADI exceedance in infants/toddlers/children and high-consuming adolescents
FDA GRAS status under GMP (21 CFR 182.1778)
JECFA group MTDI of 70 mg/kg bw/day (as phosphorus)
No specific IARC classification identified for sodium phosphates
